s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic respiratory symptoms with progressive dyspnea, fatigue, and weight loss, following a viral infection, with pleuritic chest pain and imaging findings suggestive of a pulmonary infiltrative process
salient_findings: Progressive dyspnea and chronic cough after COVID-19 infection
Pleuritic chest pain and right-sided pneumothorax
Imaging findings of parenchymal abnormalities with ground-glass halo and central cavitation
key_facts: 43-year-old woman with mild intermittent asthma
Symptoms started 6 months before presentation
Dyspnea and chronic cough after resolution of COVID-19 infection
Progressive dyspnea, fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss
No improvement with steroid taper for asthma exacerbation
Worsening shortness of breath and new pleuritic chest pain 7 days before presentation
Afebrile and mildly tachypneic at presentation
Oxygen saturation of 91% on room air
Leukocyte count 7.1 × 10⁹/L with 71% neutrophils and 0.1% eosinophils
Aspergillus IgG >200 mg/L
A. niger IgE 1.04 kU/L (weakly positive)
HIV antibody negative
TB testing (interferon-gamma release assay) negative
Serum Aspergillus galactomannan index <0.5 (negative)
No immunoglobulin deficiency on quantitative serum immunoglobulin testing

shortlist.label: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Aspergillus niger isolated from BAL, Aspergillus IgG >200 mg/L, and imaging findings suggestive of aspergilloma

shortlist.label: Aspergilloma
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of aspergilloma and suspected bronchopleural fistula, with Aspergillus niger isolated from BAL

shortlist.label: Invasive aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive dyspnea, fatigue, and weight loss, with Aspergillus niger isolated from BAL and imaging findings suggestive of invasive disease

shortlist.label: Chronic necrotizing pulmonary aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of progressive parenchymal abnormality with ground-glass halo and central cavitation, with Aspergillus niger isolated from BAL

shortlist.label: Subacute invasive aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of worsening shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain, with Aspergillus niger isolated from BAL and imaging findings suggestive of invasive disease

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of progressive dyspnea, fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss, along with the presence of Aspergillus niger in bronchoalveolar lavage and elevated Aspergillus IgG, suggest a chronic infection. The imaging studies showing interval enlargement of parenchymal abnormality with ground-glass halo and progressive central cavitation also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Aspergilloma
rejected.why: While the patient has an aspergilloma, this term typically refers to a fungal ball in a pre-existing cavity, which does not fully explain the patient's chronic and progressive symptoms.

rejected.label: Invasive aspergillosis
rejected.why: The patient's lack of fever, normal leukocyte count, and negative serum Aspergillus galactomannan index make invasive aspergillosis less likely.

rejected.label: Chronic necrotizing pulmonary aspergillosis
rejected.why: This diagnosis is possible, but the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with chronic pulmonary aspergillosis.

rejected.label: Subacute invasive aspergillosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings do not suggest a subacute invasive infection.
